summary: All three spec items are in the diff, and nothing out of scope was added. Item 1 (root cause): `_launch_kind` in shared/scripts/lib/iterate_stop_guard_background.py:40-41 now counts a truthy `resumedAgentId` or `revivedAgentId` as kind `agent`. The task is stored under the result's tool_use_id, so it gets the 2 h agent limit and is cleared by the terminal task-notification that carries the same id. Null or empty ids and a SendMessage to a running agent (no resumed field) do not count. Every regression test the spec asked for is present, built from the real resume shape, in plugins/shipwright-iterate/tests/test_iterate_stop_guard_background.py: resume after all earlier tasks finished keeps `waiting` True; the notice with the SendMessage id clears it (a `running` notice does not); the task expires after the 2 h limit; `revivedAgentId` alone is enough; the null, empty and running-agent shapes are not launches; and a whole-hook test in a real worktree checks that the guard stays quiet while the resumed agent runs and blocks again after its notice. Item 2 (message): shared/scripts/lib/iterate_stop_guard.py drops the 'contract violation' wording. It now says the iterate 'is still open', gives the Next: hint, and says waiting on a running background task is allowed (end the turn WITHOUT further tool calls). The literal `{shared_root}` placeholder is replaced by `_blocker_tool()`, which builds the absolute path from the shared scripts directory (`parents[1]/tools/record_hard_blocker.py`; I confirmed the file exists). If the path cannot be resolved it returns the bare file name instead of raising, and the new test_iterate_stop_guard_message.py covers that case. Item 3: the Stop-guard row in docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md now describes resumed and revived agents as launches. Out of scope: nothing related to the 12x Stop-hook fan-out or to the session '?' / run=unknown handling appears in the diff. I reviewed the diff only; I did not run the tests. Code-reviewer (Stage 2) may proceed.
